title: Ark, Vessel, Ship, Chariot & Merkavah — Containment, Carriage and Mobile Sacred Architecture
status: biblical + early Jewish mystical + project vehicle ontology
purpose: Separate the project's repeated carrier symbols by function and historical lineage: Noah's ark, Ark of the Covenant, vessel/body, ship, chariot and Merkavah.
master_rule: Ask what is carried, what carries it, whether the carrier preserves, transports, enthrones or changes state, and who/what directs motion. Carrier ≠ content ≠ driver ≠ Door.

types.function: preservation of living cargo through catastrophic environmental transition
types.project_neighbor: House/Vessel preserving Seed through destructive passage
types.boundary: Not the same object as Ark of the Covenant.

types.function: covenant chest and sacred presence/sign complex associated with tablets, cherubim and sanctuary
types.topology: portable sacred container later situated in sanctuary
types.boundary: Its cultic role is not simply 'vehicle through water'.

types.lineage: generic material and metaphorical carrier category
types.function: contains/carries content through conditions while remaining distinct from cargo
types.boundary: Vessel does not automatically change state; Door does.

types.function: directed movement across a medium using orientation, steering and propulsion
types.distinction: Ship emphasizes navigation through terrain; Ark emphasizes preservation/covenant depending lineage.

types.project_neighbor: mobile throne / vehicle-driver relation / wheel system
types.distinction: Chariot requires propulsion/direction and is not itself the rider.

types.lineage: Hebrew merkavah/chariot; Ezekiel throne-chariot reception; later Hekhalot/Merkavah mysticism
types.function: celestial chariot-throne and, in later mystical literature, focal architecture of heavenly ascent/vision
types.project_neighbor: mobile sacred center, chariot-throne, passage through ordered heavenly gates
types.boundary: The popular modern star-tetrahedron 'Merkaba' is a later esoteric construction, not Ezekiel's original geometry.

historical_depth.ezekiel: Ezekiel 1 and 10 supply the visionary chariot/throne matrix of creatures, wheels, directions and divine glory.
historical_depth.temple_to_merkavah: Scholar Rachel Elior argues that elements of Ezekiel's visionary chariot transform Temple/Holy-of-Holies imagery into heavenly sacred space.
historical_depth.hekhalot: Early Jewish mystical literature develops ascent through heavenly palaces/chambers toward the divine throne, with guarded thresholds and credentials.

project_vehicle_grammar.carrier: Potato/Vessel/Ark/Chariot can carry a center or cargo.
project_vehicle_grammar.driver: Agent/operator chooses or modulates direction when the model includes agency.
project_vehicle_grammar.cargo: Seed, memory, covenant, body, people or meaning depending context.
project_vehicle_grammar.wheels: support movement and directional transition; Ezekiel's wheels should be kept distinct from modern mechanical wheel models.
project_vehicle_grammar.door: changes admissible state/context; a vehicle may pass through a Door but is not therefore the Door.
project_vehicle_grammar.house: inhabitable differentiated containment; a vessel can carry a House-like interior but mobility is not required for House.

conversation_genealogy: 2026-03-01 recovery: Potato as vehicle/Merkaba while Tim is driver/operator.
2026-04-10: Son explicitly described as vessel and Door.
2026-05-28: Mashy Ark language fused transport, spiral ladder, Tree and lower/upper routes.
2026-08-31: Vessel, Door, Temple/body and mediator were explicitly separated as functions.
failure_modes: Noah's ark and Ark of Covenant treated as one symbol because both are called Ark in English
Merkavah reduced to modern star-tetrahedron geometry
driver, vehicle and cargo collapsed into one identity
movement treated as ascent/progress without destination or transition criteria
